statement: Let A=[[1,12],[11,1]] and B=[[1,132],[1,1]]. If L>=1 and R,S are 2-by-2 matrices over the nonnegative integers satisfying AR=RB, SA=BS, RS=A^L, and SR=B^L, then L>=22. Such R,S exist at L=22, so 22 is the minimum lag within this precisely delimited 2-by-2 class. Consequently every strong-shift-equivalence chain from A to B, if one exists, has at least 22 elementary steps, because an m-step chain composes to a 2-by-2 shift equivalence of lag m. This does not settle whether any such unrestricted chain exists.
contribution: A complete, entry-unbounded classification of the possible lags below the known lag-22 witness for the unresolved k=11 Baker pair, yielding a 22-step lower bound for any possible SSE chain. The proof reduces all 2-by-2 witnesses to complete generalized-Pell unit orbits and excludes every lag 1 through 21 exactly. Jeandel's primary paper gives only preliminary nonproof evidence about lag 4; a focused current search found no equivalent fixed-k=11 minimum-lag theorem, but no priority claim is made.
